changes: lattice.config.json: removed the duplicated bare-string validate.commands entry for reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js, keeping the focus-tagged object form. validate.commands went from 48 to 47 entries; the smoke is now registered exactly once.
usage: Run lattice validate (or node bin/lattice.js validate --json in a worktree). The reviewer-scan-budget-guard smoke now executes once per unfocused run instead of twice, and validate --focus=fast still selects it.
expectedOutcome: A completed validate invocation record contains exactly one command result referencing reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js, and it passes.
actualTranscript: validate --json produced 47 command results; exactly one referenced reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js with code:0 and output "reviewer-scan-budget-guard: PASS (6 prompt copies clean, 7 required phrases present)". The stderr per-command record independently showed one start and one end line for that script; a second run reproduced the count of one.
outcomeDiff: No difference: expected exactly one passing invocation, observed exactly one passing invocation.
limitations: none — fully covered. The change is a strict superset-preserving deletion; the smoke script and the validate runner implementation were not touched.
pitfalls: The host was under heavy load from other parallel Lattice sessions (load average peaked ~392, 40+ node processes). Under that load two UNRELATED validate commands failed on timing: validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.js (timed out waiting for a fixture file) and quorum-submit-smoke.js (exceeded its 600s per-command budget). Both pass standalone and are not caused by this change. Also: the 47-command validate list does not fit the default 900s CLI watchdog on this host — one entry alone budgets 600s — so validate and TEST/DONE gates need LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS raised (e.g. 3600000) when the machine is busy. And the global lattice binary is blocked in worktrees (stale_global_runtime_in_worktree); use node bin/lattice.js after building the worktree runtime.
